website_review.search_basics: Search results show category pages (/flowers, /plants, /get-well), product pages and an /about-us and /faq page with delivery and fee text, which is a healthy structure for a florist; JSON-LD could not be verified.

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: GBP has category 'Florist', address, hours ('Closed · Opens 9 AM'), phone and the website, but it is unclaimed ('Claim this business') and I could not read a review count. Answerable: delivery area, same-day cut-off, $10 fee and $40 minimum appear as text on /about-us and /faq per search results; schema presence unverified because the site blocked my browser. Bookable: ordering happens through the Teleflora-hosted checkout, not a booking platform — an agent can plausibly order flowers but scheduling/availability could not be tested.

operations_signals.signal: Fixed delivery rules (1 p.m. cut-off, no Sunday, $10 fee, $40 minimum) mean repetitive phone questions about eligibility and timing
Order flow runs through a Teleflora storefront, so the shop shares margin and does not own its customer data or reorder channel (inference)
Unclaimed Google profile for a very long-established shop leaves review replies and photos unmanaged

top_opportunities.evidence: Listing shows 'Claim this business' and offers no review count or services in the view I loaded

top_opportunities.evidence: Delivery rules exist only as prose on /about-us and /faq, and the shop's own advice is to call (732) 257-2357

top_opportunities.evidence: Inference: the catalogue and checkout run on the Teleflora platform, so the shop does not own the customer relationship

scores.reasons: The storefront looks reasonably complete (Teleflora catalogue, FAQ, delivery rules), so gaps are an unclaimed profile and phone-bound service questions. Florist economics are small-ticket with a $40 minimum. Ease is middling because the site is a vendor platform I could not inspect. Confidence is the lowest in this batch: Cloudflare blocked my browser, so the website review rests on search-result text.

caveats: Google review counts were read from the Maps result panel; for Trygar's Hardware and Main Street Florist the panel loaded in a limited view that showed a rating but no review count, so those counts are marked as not shown rather than guessed.

Google's 'Claim this business' prompt was used as the signal for an unclaimed profile. Where the prompt was absent I treat the profile as claimed, but I could not confirm ownership from the business side.

Trygar's Hardware serves the same one-page site on trygar.com and keysthatplease.com; HTTPS on trygar.com fails certificate validation, so the content was read over plain HTTP and the mobile screenshot was taken with certificate errors ignored for that page only.

Main Street Florist's site is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge that I did not attempt to bypass; its website review is based on search-result text plus the Google listing, not a direct read. Its phone_layout value of 'broken' means 'not loadable for a customer check in my browser', not a confirmed customer-facing fault.

Fred's Towing has no owned website; the Google profile links to facebook.com generically and I did not find a confirmed Facebook page for the South River business. fredstowing.com belongs to a different company in Henderson, NC and was excluded.
data_gaps: Main Street Florist: Cloudflare 'Performing security verification' interstitial on two attempts plus a 403 on a direct HTTP fetch; desktop and mobile rendering, schema markup, title/description tags and checkout flow could not be inspected.
Main Street Florist and Trygar's Hardware: Google review counts were not displayed in the limited Maps view; review themes therefore not assessed for those two.
robots.txt could not be read for Beyond Automotive (HTTP 406) or Trygar's Hardware (HTTPS broken); no blocking rules were observed via any other route.
Globo Auto: contact-form delivery could not be verified without submitting the form, which is out of scope; the form has no action attribute and no visible handler in the page source.
No payroll, revenue, fleet-size or headcount data was available for any business in this batch; size signals are limited to review counts, years in business, published staff names and site content.
